card.architecture: Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B diffusion transformer (umT5 encoder) — IMAGE-TO-VIDEO + per-frame PixelQuantize
card.summary: Pixel-art image-to-video (locked-palette per-frame quantize). Animates a still image into a short clip (image-to-video). The 5B TI2V model fits 8GB via the Q4_K_M GGUF + native offload. Edit-only: pick it in the editor, describe the motion, get an animated WEBP back. — 24 GB build: fp16.
use_cases: animate a photo or generated image into a short clip
add camera motion or subtle subject movement to a still
card.pick_when: You want to turn a still image into a short video clip.

prompt.guidance: Describe the MOTION and what should happen in the clip (a camera move, the subject's action). The source image is the first frame.
prompt.example: the camera slowly pushes in as her hair drifts in a gentle breeze
prompt.overview: The uploaded image is the first frame, so write a detailed natural-language prompt describing only how the visible subject and camera MOVE (motion + camera + speed + atmosphere), not what things look like.
prompt.instructions: Wan 2.2 responds best to detailed, structured natural-language prompts (target ~80-120 words) built in layers: Subject/Scene, then Motion (what moves and how), then Camera movement (pan, tilt, dolly, orbit, crane, push-in/zoom), then Speed/Intensity (slow, gentle, brisk, whip-pan, slow-motion), then Atmosphere/Aesthetics (lighting, color grade, lens, mood). For i2v, skip or minimize subject description because the image defines appearance, and animate only elements actually visible in the frame, putting the most important motion early since Wan weights the start of the prompt more heavily. Always pair with a negative prompt, which Wan 2.2 enforces more reliably than 2.1.
do: Lead with the primary motion using concrete verbs with explicit speed and direction ('slowly turns her head left')
Specify a distinct camera move (slow push-in, dolly out, pan left, clockwise orbit, crane up, static)
State speed/intensity explicitly (gentle, subtle, gradual, rapid, slow-motion)
Add atmosphere and aesthetic control: lighting, color grade, lens/shot type, weather, mood
Put the most important detail early; Wan 2.2 weights the beginning of the prompt
Keep it detailed but bounded, ~80-120 words, and always include a negative prompt
Describe only motion of elements visible in the source image
dont: Don't re-describe the subject's static appearance in i2v (the image already defines it)
Don't introduce objects, characters, or scenery not present in the source frame
Don't use vague generic action verbs without speed/direction ('it moves', 'things happen')
Don't overload with so many details that key motion gets ignored (avoid >120 words)
Don't omit the negative prompt or assume the model avoids artifacts on its own
examples: The woman slowly turns her head to the left while maintaining eye contact with the camera, her hair drifting gently in a light breeze. Slow push-in on her face, shallow depth of field. Soft window light shifts subtly across her skin, warm color grade, calm and intimate mood, gentle pacing throughout.

The mech's chest panels hiss open and steam vents to the sides as it raises one arm toward the camera. The camera slowly dollies out and tilts up to reveal its full height. Sparks fall in the foreground, harsh industrial overhead lighting, cool blue-grey color grade, deliberate and weighty motion.
prompt.negative_guidance: Wan 2.2 enforces negatives more reliably than 2.1; the canonical default is the Chinese string shipped in the official Wan repo/ComfyUI workflows: 色调艳丽，过曝，静态，细节模糊不清，字幕，风格，作品，画作，画面，静止，整体发灰，最差质量，低质量，JPEG压缩残留，丑陋的，残缺的，多余的手指，画得不好的手部，画得不好的脸部，畸形的，毁容的，形态畸形的肢体，手指融合，静止不动的画面，杂乱的背景，三条腿，背景人很多，倒着走 . For video, add terms like morphing, warping, distortion, flickering, jittering, face deformation, sudden changes.

ui_help.note: Animate the current picture: describe the motion you want (a camera move, the subject's action). The picture becomes the first frame.
ui_help.good_for: turning a still image into a short video
